excerpt: Truv verifies income, employment and assets through consumer-permissioned payroll and bank data. Checkr announced it had acquired Truv in August 2026.
content:
Truv is a US company that verifies a person's income, employment and assets using data the consumer gives permission to share. Instead of collecting pay stubs, a lender or agency sends the applicant a Truv link; the applicant logs in to their payroll provider, employer or bank, and Truv returns the verified data through an API. Its website lists products for mortgage lending (including income, employment and asset verification and employment reverification), consumer and auto lending, tenant and background screening, retail banking (such as direct deposit switching) and the public sector, where it verifies income for benefits programmes. It also offers document upload and document fraud detection for cases where a direct connection is not possible.

Acquisition by Checkr

On 18 August 2026 the background-check company Checkr announced that it had acquired Truv. Terms were not disclosed. Checkr said the deal strengthens its mortgage business and marks its entry into government work through benefits eligibility checks, since Truv already serves state agencies running social services programmes. Checkr said Truv's network reaches 96% of the US workforce. Kirill Klokov is Truv's co-founder and CEO. HousingWire and PYMNTS covered the deal.

Pricing

Truv's pricing page names three plans, Launch, Professional and Enterprise, but shows no dollar figures. It says Truv charges per successful connection, however many times the data is pulled afterwards, that pay-as-you-go has no spending minimum, and that annual commitments on Professional and Enterprise come with guaranteed savings of 35% and 70% or more respectively. Exact rates come from sales.

Who it suits

Truv is built for mortgage lenders, consumer and auto lenders, screening companies, banks and government agencies in the US that verify income at volume. It is not a consumer app; individuals meet it only when a lender or agency sends them a link.

This page draws on Truv's website and pricing page (checked 15 October 2026), Checkr's announcement and coverage in HousingWire and PYMNTS.
